samples.summary: Stale `undoJumpTarget` is re-applied after any SheetView remount other than a history restore
samples.evidence: `undoJumpTarget` is only ever cleared in `handleHistoryRestored` (document-detail.tsx:182). `SheetView` remembers the handled request in a mount-local ref (`lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef`, sheet-view.tsx:244), which resets to 0 on any unmount/remount — and `historyResetToken` is not the only remount: `SheetView` is unmounted whenever the active tab is a datasource (document-detail.tsx:746) or lakehouse (751) tab, and whenever `!ready || !activeTabId` swaps in the `Loader` (744). Sequence: a cross-tab undo jumps to Sheet2 and is handled; the user clicks a datasource tab (SheetView unmounts) and then returns to Sheet2; the effect at sheet-view.tsx:1443 sees a non-null `undoJumpTarget` whose `requestId` (>0) no longer matches the fresh ref (0), so it calls `focusUndoSelection` again and hijacks/scrolls the user's selection to a long-past undo. The in-code justification ("`historyResetToken` remounts `SheetView`") assumes that is the only remount, which the datasource/lakehouse/Loader branches contradict.

samples.summary: The shared sheet view passes no `onUndoJump`, so cross-tab undo is invisible for editor-role share links — and the prop's stated justification is false
samples.evidence: sheet-view.tsx's `onUndoJump` doc-comment claims it may be "omitted (the read-only share view) ... which is moot there since undo is disabled". But `shared-document.tsx:198` computes `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, so an `editor`-role share link renders `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} readOnly={false} peerJumpTarget={...} />` (line 300) with undo fully enabled and no `onUndoJump`. In that surface an undo whose step belongs to another tab mutates the CRDT and neither switches tabs nor moves the selection — exactly the "undo looks like it did nothing" defect this change exists to fix, left in place on one of two sheet surfaces, with an inline comment asserting it cannot happen.

samples.summary: An undo touching both row and column axis metadata resolves to no selection at all
samples.evidence: The header branches are mutually exclusive: `if (touch.rows.size > 0 && touch.columns.size === 0)` (444) and `if (touch.columns.size > 0 && touch.rows.size === 0)` (456). A single undo step that wrote both `rowHeights`/`rowStyles` and `colWidths`/`colStyles` (e.g. an autofit or a batched resize over a block selection, or a row+column style application) satisfies neither, has no `cells` entries, and falls through to the final `return { tabId, otherTab, selectionType: 'cell' }` with no `range` — so `Sheet.applyUndoSelection` returns early and the selection never moves, which is the original reported defect for that class of edit.

samples.summary: `diffAxisSpan` mis-handles axis edits at the tail and combined middle-insert + append
samples.evidence: `if (head === shorter) return undefined;` (276) treats any change confined to the array tail as "the axis merely grew to reach a cell". Undoing a delete of the *last* rows/columns (ids re-appended at the tail) therefore reports no structural span, so the undo selects the restored cells as a cell range instead of the row/column headers (acknowledged in docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-undo-selection-todo.md:183, but still wrong output). Separately, a step that inserts in the middle *and* appends at the tail defeats the common-suffix loop (`tail` stays 0), so `changed = after.length - head` over-counts and the reported span runs from the insertion point all the way to the end of the axis.

samples.summary: Nested operation paths (`rowStyles.<idx>`, `colStyles.<idx>`, cell sub-fields) fall through to the no-coordinate branch
samples.evidence: The `switch (parsed.rest)` only matches exact segment names, and the cell extraction only handles `cells` / `cells.<cellKey>`. A write that reaches inside a style object — path `$.sheets.<tab>.rowStyles.3` with key `bold`, or `$.sheets.<tab>.cells.r3|c1.style` with key `bold` — yields `rest = 'rowStyles.3'` (no case match → `default`) or `cellKey = 'r3|c1.style'` (unresolvable by `parseWorksheetCellKey`, then `continue` at line 184, discarding the op). Both produce a selection with no `range`, so those undos leave the cursor where it was.
searchedFor: grep for cells[ writes in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet

samples.summary: `pickTab` can pick the current tab on a coordinate-less touch and suppress the cross-tab jump entirely
samples.evidence: `const current = touches.get(currentTabId); if (current) return current;` (243-244) returns the current tab whenever it received *any* op, including one that lands in the `default` branch (charts, comments, freeze pane, filters) and carries no coordinates. If the real cell change of that undo step happened in another tab, the resolver then returns `{ tabId: current, otherTab: false }` with no `range`: no tab switch fires and the selection does not move, so the undo again "looks like it did nothing" — the exact case the feature targets.

samples.summary: `undo()`/`redo()` scroll the current tab even when the replayed step landed in another tab
samples.evidence: `this.worksheet.revealActiveCell()` (654 and the redo twin at 667) is called unconditionally after a successful replay. When `UndoSelection.otherTab` is true, `Sheet.applyUndoSelection` deliberately leaves this tab's selection untouched and only fires `onUndoTabJump`; the reveal then scrolls the current viewport back to the pre-existing active cell for no reason, which is visible if the user had scrolled away.

verdict.reason: Code matches the finding exactly. `undoJumpTarget` is cleared only in `handleHistoryRestored` (document-detail.tsx:182); `SheetView` is keyed solely by `historyResetToken` (758) yet is fully unmounted on the datasource (746-750), lakehouse (751-755) and Loader (744-745) branches, so a remount can occur without any restore. The dedupe ref `lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef` is mount-local (`useRef(0)`, sheet-view.tsx:244), so after such a remount the effect at sheet-view.tsx:1443-1455 sees requestId != 0 and re-invokes `sheet.focusUndoSelection`, which changes selection, re-renders and scrolls via `revealActiveCell()` (spreadsheet.ts:689-707). No other guard clears or re-syncs the target on tab switch (only setters at 161/182). Reachable in normal use; user-visible selection hijack — major.

finding.summary: The shared sheet view passes no `onUndoJump`, so cross-tab undo is invisible for editor-role share links — and the prop's stated justification is false
finding.evidence: sheet-view.tsx's `onUndoJump` doc-comment claims it may be "omitted (the read-only share view) ... which is moot there since undo is disabled". But `shared-document.tsx:198` computes `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, so an `editor`-role share link renders `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} readOnly={false} peerJumpTarget={...} />` (line 300) with undo fully enabled and no `onUndoJump`. In that surface an undo whose step belongs to another tab mutates the CRDT and neither switches tabs nor moves the selection — exactly the "undo looks like it did nothing" defect this change exists to fix, left in place on one of two sheet surfaces, with an inline comment asserting it cannot happen.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and reachable. Repo-wide grep shows `onUndoJump` is supplied at exactly one call site (document-detail.tsx:763); the only other SheetView mount, shared-document.tsx:300, passes neither `onUndoJump` nor `undoJumpTarget` while `readOnly` is false for an `editor`-role share token (shared-document.tsx:198). That layout renders a tab bar and lets the visitor switch and edit multiple tabs (shared-document.tsx:305-315), and editor tokens really do carry write access (share-link.service.ts:79-86). Undo is live because the engine gates edits only on `_readOnly` (spreadsheet.ts:119,1036), and the store resolves `otherTab` against document-wide Yorkie history (yorkie-store.ts:1276-1333; undo-selection.ts:394). When a replayed step belongs to another tab, sheet.ts:5489-5491 returns early after calling `onUndoTabJump`, which sheet-view.tsx:1082-1084 forwards to an undefined `onUndoJumpRef.current?.(...)` — the CRDT mutates while the view neither switches tabs nor moves selection, i.e. the "undo looks like it did nothing" defect persists on this surface. The prop's doc-comment at sheet-view.tsx:162-168 asserting the omission is "moot there since undo is disabled" is false for the editor role. Correctness lane: wrong/silent behavior on a normally reachable path; major.
